findings.finding: Fixed length curriculum restores original delayed-noise task learning in three fresh seeds; removal of payload alone is not consistently sufficient.
With IID learning resolved and resources matched, independent blocks lose to random masks at primary delay32; the registered useful-gain prediction is falsified.
Zeroing distractor payload harms both frozen models and collapses the matched control, invalidating the apparent gap closure; the paired interaction also spans zero.
The registered >=5pp uncued linear-access deficit is excluded while both frozen states remain near-perfectly decodable and their original task readouts still differ.
Across ten trained seeds the block model has a positive excess short-to-long fixed-ridge prior-answer transfer loss; the >=5pp minimum is not confirmed.
The final revised label is highly linearly readable in both frozen models, but the registered >=3pp model gap remains uncertain with a paired interval crossing zero and threshold.
